findings.description: The new repo-root containment check does not examine the path that is actually written. `real_archive_path` is built from `${archive_path##*/}`, i.e. only the basename of `archive_path`, so any directory components contributed by the ledger-derived `cycle_id` (used earlier as `archive_path="${ARCHIVE_DIR}/${cycle_id}"`) are discarded before the `== "$root_real"/*` test. `cycle_id` comes from `ledger.json` `.id` and the diff shows no sanitisation of it beyond the numeric check on `cycle`; the test suite deliberately exercises free-form suffixes such as `cycle-098-foo`. A ledger id like `cycle-120-x/../../..` therefore passes the check, `mkdir -p`/`cp` operate outside the archive directory (e.g. overwriting files under `grimoires/`), the WARN never fires, and the ledger records a misleading relative `archive_path`.
findings.failure_mode: A crafted or corrupted `ledger.json` (e.g. from a cloned repository) can steer the archive writes to an arbitrary location relative to the repo, while the new root-containment logic reports the archive as safely inside the repo and persists a false `archive_path` into the ledger.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate `cycle_id` before using it as a path segment (e.g. reject anything not matching `^cycle-[0-9]+[A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`, and reject `/`, `..`). Compute containment on the real target: `real_archive_path=$(cd "$(dirname "$archive_path")" && pwd -P)/$(basename "$archive_path")`, or better, resolve `realpath -m "$archive_path"` and require it to be strictly under `$archive_dir_real`.

findings.description: The tracked-archive protection is gated on `git -C "$ARCHIVE_DIR" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` succeeding. Any git failure (dubious-ownership refusal when the checkout is owned by a different uid, a missing or corrupt `.git`, a `safe.directory` policy, a broken PATH git) is indistinguishable from "not a work tree" and silently sets `in_git=false`, so the mtime-only `rm -rf` path runs against directories that are in fact tracked. `_archive_dir_tracked` itself is written fail-safe (any rc other than 1 counts as tracked), but the outer detection is fail-open, defeating that care.
findings.failure_mode: In a container or CI checkout where git refuses to operate, a run with retention > 0 deletes git-tracked archive history without the promised `[WARN] tracked archive kept` message.
findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish "not a repo" (rev-parse exit 128 with `not a git repository`) from other git errors; on any other failure, WARN and skip deletion entirely (fail-safe), or require `--force` to prune when git state cannot be verified.

findings.description: `parse_args` still swallows unknown options with `*) shift ;;`. The diff adds `--force` and makes the script perform irreversible actions (ledger mutation, `rm -rf` of archives when retention is set), so a mistyped safety flag such as `--dry_run`, `--dryrun` or `--retention=3` is silently ignored and the run proceeds as a real archive and prune instead of failing fast.
findings.failure_mode: Operator or agent intends a preview or a specific retention but a typo causes a live archive, ledger write, and possible deletion of untracked archive directories.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the default case to `echo "ERROR: unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1` and accept `--opt=value` forms explicitly.

findings.description: The completeness gate (`_count_incomplete_sprints`), the `cycle_id` resolution, and the copy of `ledger.json` into the archive all read the ledger without holding the `ledger-lib.sh` lock; only the final `_update_ledger_archived` takes the lock. Two concurrent invocations (or a concurrent sprint-status update) can both pass the gate, both write into the same `archive_path`, and the archived `ledger.json` snapshot may not match the state the lock-protected update is applied to.
findings.failure_mode: Concurrent runs produce a corrupted or interleaved archive directory and a snapshot that does not correspond to the recorded ledger transition; the gate can be bypassed by a status change racing the check.
findings.suggested_fix: Acquire `_lock_ledger_transaction` before the gate check and hold it through the archive copy and ledger write (the lock already lives in a subshell; move the whole non-dry-run body into it), or re-verify the gate under the lock inside `_update_ledger_archived` and abort if it no longer holds.
